content.title: About
content.content: Gluten free plain crackers are crisp, dry biscuits made from gluten‑free grains such as rice, corn or potato starch and a pinch of salt. They contain no wheat, barley or rye, making them suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity. Their neutral flavor makes them a versatile base for toppings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Gluten‑free crackers are a staple in many low‑gluten diets because they pair well with a variety of spreads.
Rice flour is commonly used, giving the crackers a light, airy texture.
Because they lack gluten, they reduce the risk of allergic reactions in celiac individuals.
Plain crackers are often used in culinary schools to test new sauces and toppings.
Some brands add seeds (e.g., pumpkin) to boost flavor and nutritional value.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Most gluten‑free crackers are baked with minimal oil, making them less calorie‑dense than many traditional snacks.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Rice or corn‑based crackers provide slow‑releasing energy, helping to maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Suitable for individuals with celiac disease, gluten intolerance, or those following a gluten‑free diet.

items.title: Easily digestible
items.content: The neutral composition makes them a gentle option for those with digestive sensitivities.

items.title: Moderate sodium
items.content: A modest amount of salt helps maintain electrolyte balance without excessive sodium intake.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Some gluten‑free crackers may contain soy, dairy or nuts, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Rice‑based crackers can raise blood sugar quickly, which may be a concern for diabetics.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Although usually moderate, people with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Added additives
items.content: Certain brands use flavor enhancers such as monosodium glutamate, which some individuals prefer to avoid.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Gluten free crackers can be enjoyed plain, spread with hummus, cream cheese, avocado, or used as a base for canapés. They also add a crunchy topping to soups and salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in the sealed package. After opening, transfer to an airtight container to prevent moisture absorption. Follow the “best before” date on the packaging.
